title: Enhancing iNKT cell immunotherapy through the integration of optimized CAR endodomains and iNKT engagers
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76718-7

iNKT cells are a subset of T cells with both innate and adaptive features, emerging as a promising immunotherapy platform due to their rapid response. Here, the authors develop a CAR-iNKT strategy incorporating a CD28ζ co-stimulatory domain and two bispecific iNKT engagers to enhance multiple myeloma targeting.

title: Macroscopic chirogenesis and photoinduced chiral motions enabled by selective accommodation of protic guests
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76735-6

Symmetry breaking offers ideal platforms for understanding the emergence of chirality in bottom-up self-assembly. Here the authors show the chirogenesis induced by symmetry breaking through selective entrapping solvent guests and photoinduced motions in self-assembled matrices.

title: Correlated insulating states in slow Dirac fermions on a honeycomb moiré superlattice
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76783-y

Transition metal dichalcogenide twisted structures are known to exhibit strongly correlated phenomena. Here, the authors demonstrate a range of correlated insulating states at integer and fractional fillings in twisted MoSe2 homobilayers arising from the Γ-valley moire flat bands.

title: Endothelial cell-microglia crosstalk mediates heart failure-associated synaptic loss and cognitive impairment in male mice
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76687-x

Cardiac failure is associated with cognitive impairment. Here, the authors show that blood-borne signals can induce brain endothelial cell-release of SPARC, resulting in the activation of microglia, synapse loss, and cognitive decline following transverse aortic constriction in mice.

title: Interpretable self-driving sputtering epitaxy reveals human-usable growth rules for β-Ga2O3 films
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76533-0

Materials growth requires navigating complex conditions. Here, the authors combine automated sputtering, Bayesian optimization, and interpretable machine learning in a self-driving laboratory to optimize β-Ga2O3 growth and extract practical rules.

title: Strategic objectives underpin national climate pledges
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76467-7

Countries use international climate pledges not only to express domestic policy preferences, but to advance strategic goals like attracting finance, enhancing status, and setting standards for others. These objectives have important implications for ambition.

title: Extreme vulnerability to intruder attacks destabilizes network dynamics
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76342-5

A single malicious agent can destabilize an entire network by targeting a low-connectivity node. Here, authors show that these nodes are more vulnerable than highly connected hubs, revealing an intrinsic weakness shared by technological, biological, and social networks.
